intro.en: Comprehensive practical examination guide covering obstetrics and gynaecological instruments, cervical sampling and cytology methods, laparoscopy equipment, and hysteroscopic assemblies.

items.summary: A double-ended, non-self-retaining metallic speculum designed to retract the posterior vaginal wall.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Double-ended metal speculum with two duckbill blades of unequal size directed at right angles to a central trough-like handle.
The central shank connects the blades and features a grooved gutter that allows collected discharge or blood to drain away.
Requires manual retraction by an assistant during clinical examination or operative procedures.

groups.label: Outpatient department
bullets: Retracts posterior vaginal wall to visualise cervix, cervical erosion, ectropion, polyp, ulcer, or frank malignant growth.
Enables visual evaluation of anterior and posterior vaginal wall prolapse as well as post-hysterectomy vault prolapse.
Visualises cervix during cervical smear collection, liquid-based cytology, and endocervical microbiological swab sampling.
Facilitates visualisation for intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) insertion, levonorgestrel system placement, or string retrieval.
Aids visualisation during outpatient Pipelle endometrial biopsy, cervical punch biopsy, colposcopy, and hysterosalpingography (HSG).

groups.label: Labour ward
bullets: Visual inspection of cervix and vagina to identify local causes of antepartum haemorrhage (APH).
Aids speculum examination to confirm preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) by pooling of liquor.
Visual inspection of cervix and vaginal vault for traumatic lacerations following instrumental delivery or difficult childbirth.
Visualisation during surgical evacuation of uterus for incomplete abortion or medical termination of pregnancy (MTP).

groups.label: Operation theatre
bullets: Essential retractor in vaginal hysterectomy, pelvic floor repair, and Manchester-Fothergill surgery.
Used in diagnostic hysteroscopy, cervical cerclage, diagnostic laparoscopy with chromopertubation, fractional curettage, and polypectomy.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Sims position (left lateral semi-prone position): patient lies on left side with buttocks at couch edge, right hip and knee acutely flexed.
Demerit is that it is non-self-retaining and strictly requires an assistant to hold it in place.
Sims triad comprises Sims speculum, Sims position, and surgical repair of rectovaginal or vesicovaginal fistula.
Examination can be hindered if the patient is not brought right to the edge of the examining table.

viva.q: What is the primary function of Sims speculum?
viva.a: It retracts the posterior vaginal wall to expose the cervix and anterior vaginal wall for diagnostic inspection and operative interventions.

viva.q: Why does Sims speculum require an assistant?
viva.a: Because it is a non-self-retaining instrument, requiring manual upward and backward traction to keep the posterior vaginal wall retracted.

viva.q: What is Sims position and why is it used?
viva.a: A left lateral semi-prone posture where the pelvis tilts forward, allowing atmospheric air to distend the vagina and enhance cervical visualisation.

image.brief: Metallic double-ended Sims speculum laid on a flat white background showing two curved blades of different breadths connected by a grooved central handle.

items.summary: A self-retaining bivalve vaginal speculum with adjustable hinged blades and a thumbscrew mechanism for cervical exposure.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Consists of two hinged metal or clear plastic blades oriented along an axis perpendicular to the handle.
Equipped with a screw and ratchet mechanism on the handle that opens, spreads, and locks the blades at the desired aperture.
Self-retaining mechanism holds the vaginal walls apart without needing an assistant.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Routine outpatient visualisation of cervix for cervical erosion, ectropion, polyp, ulcer, or suspicious growth.
Obtaining cervical Papanicolaou (Pap) smear, liquid-based cytology (LBC), and high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) samples.
Visualising external os during insertion or removal of copper intrauterine contraceptive devices (IUCD) or levonorgestrel systems.
Direct visualisation for outpatient endocervical swab taking, colposcopy, punch biopsy, and Pipelle endometrial sampling.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Key advantage over Sims speculum is being self-retaining, leaving both of the clinician hands free to conduct procedures.
Can be used with the patient positioned centrally on an examination couch without needing the buttocks over the table edge.
Major limitation: cannot assess anterior or posterior vaginal wall prolapse because the blades conceal the vaginal walls.
Available in stainless steel reusable form and disposable clear plastic models.

viva.q: What is the chief advantage of Cusco speculum over Sims speculum?
viva.a: It is self-retaining, freeing both hands of the clinician to take smears or perform procedures without needing an assistant.

viva.q: Why is Cusco speculum unsuitable for assessing pelvic organ prolapse?
viva.a: The rigid anterior and posterior blades conceal the vaginal walls, preventing dynamic evaluation of cystocele and rectocele during straining.

image.brief: Bivalve metallic Cusco speculum shown in three-quarter view on a white background with open duckbill blades and visible thumbscrew mechanism on handle.

items.summary: A slender double-ended instrument with angled fenestrated loops designed to push back a lax anterior vaginal wall.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Features a long, thin central shaft ending in two fenestrated oval loops set at approximately 15 degrees to the shaft.
The terminal loops point in opposite directions and bear transverse serrations across their rims.
The surface serrations engage vaginal mucosal rugosities to prevent slippage during retraction.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Used together with Sims speculum to retract a redundant, lax anterior vaginal wall that bulges into view and hides the cervix.
Improves cervical exposure during outpatient examinations, cervical smear collection, and vaginal surgical repairs.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Must not be confused with a uterine curette; the retractor has broad serrated loops rather than a sharp or blunt scoop.
The 15-degree angulation of the loops allows the operator hand to stay clear of the visual line of sight.
Requires delicate handling to avoid pinching the anterior vaginal mucosa against the pubic bone.

viva.q: Why does the Sims anterior vaginal wall retractor have serrations on its loops?
viva.a: The serrations grip the transverse vaginal rugosities securely, preventing the instrument from slipping over the moist mucosa.

viva.q: How do you distinguish this instrument from a uterine curette?
viva.a: The retractor features large, serrated fenestrated loops angled at fifteen degrees, unlike the smaller smooth sharp or blunt cup of a curette.

image.brief: Slender metallic anterior vaginal wall retractor laid on a plain white backdrop highlighting opposite-facing angled fenestrated oval ends with serrations.

credit.generated: Illustration created with MaiK (StewardMD AI) and checked against the real instrument shape

items.summary: A heavy ratcheted grasping forceps with curved shanks and multiple interlocking teeth on each blade for steadying the cervix.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Long scissor-type instrument with finger ring handles, a ratchet lock, and curved or straight shanks.
Each jaw terminates in multiple sharp inward-curving teeth that interlock firmly when closed.
The blades bow outward to leave a clearance space, preventing crushing of grasped cervical tissue.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Grasping and applying downward traction on the anterior lip of the cervix in gynaecological operations.
Used in vaginal hysterectomy, Manchester-Fothergill repair, anterior colporrhaphy, and posterior colpoperineorrhaphy.
Steadying the cervix during cervical polypectomy, colpotomy, cervical biopsy, and cryosurgery.
Used during diagnostic dilation and curettage (D&C) and performing the vulsellum traction test to evaluate uterine descent.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Contraindicated on the gravid or puerperal cervix because vascular, softened tissue tears easily under sharp teeth.
Less traumatic than a single-toothed tenaculum because traction force is distributed across multiple prongs.
The curve in the handle enables better visualisation of the cervix while using the instrument.

viva.q: Why is the vulsellum avoided during pregnancy and postpartum procedures?
viva.a: The gravid cervix is soft, hypervascular, and friable; the sharp multiple teeth easily tear through tissue and provoke heavy bleeding.

viva.q: What is the vulsellum traction test?
viva.a: Applying gentle downward traction on the cervix under anaesthesia to demonstrate the true extent of uterine and vaginal vault descent.

image.brief: Metallic Teale vulsellum forceps displayed on a neutral background with curved shanks, ratcheted ring handles, and multiple interlocking sharp teeth at the jaws.

items.summary: A ratcheted grasping forceps terminating in a single sharp, inward-pointing hook on each blade for securing the cervix.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Features scissor-like finger ring handles with an articulating ratchet lock and slender straight or curved shanks.
Working tip consists of a single fine, sharp hook on each jaw that penetrates and meets the opposing hook.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Holding the anterior lip of the cervix steady during intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) insertion or removal.
Fixing the cervix in nulliparous women with a conical cervix before hysterosalpingography (HSG) cannula placement.
Steadying the cervix during outpatient cervical punch biopsy and cryocautery procedures.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Penetrates deeper into cervical stroma than vulsellum, making it more traumatic if forceful traction is exerted.
Ideal for gripping a small, smooth, conical nulliparous cervix where a multi-toothed vulsellum might slip.
Contraindicated on the gravid or infected cervix due to high risk of bleeding and tissue laceration.

viva.q: When is a tenaculum preferred over a vulsellum?
viva.a: In nulliparous women with a small, firm, conical cervix where single sharp hooks obtain purchase without slipping.

viva.q: Why is tenaculum traction risky on a pregnant cervix?
viva.a: The softened tissue offers minimal structural resistance, causing the single pointed tooth to slice through the cervix and produce haemorrhage.

image.brief: Single-toothed tenaculum forceps on a plain white surface showcasing ring handles, ratchet lock, and jaws with opposed sharp curved single points.

items.summary: A long atraumatic forceps with serrated oval fenestrated tips designed for swab application and non-crushing tissue handling.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Long-shafted instrument with scissor handles, a sturdy ratchet lock, and straight or slightly curved shanks.
Jaws end in smooth, oval, fenestrated loops lined with fine horizontal serrations to grip gauze or swabs securely.
Completely atraumatic tips that grasp delicate tissues without puncturing or tearing.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Holding gauze swabs soaked in antiseptic solution for surgical skin preparation and vaginal decontamination.
Grasping and steadying the soft, vascular pregnant cervix during suction evacuation or cervical cerclage placement.
Systematic inspection of the cervix following instrumental vaginal delivery to identify occult lacerations.
Holding the margins of the lower uterine segment incision during caesarean birth to promote haemostasis before suturing.
Mopping blood and exudate from deep surgical pelvic pockets to maintain a clear operative view.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: The standard atraumatic instrument of choice for grasping the gravid cervix because it avoids stromal laceration.
Ubiquitously employed across obstetric, gynaecological, and general surgical procedures.

viva.q: Why is sponge holding forceps chosen over vulsellum to grasp the cervix during cervical cerclage?
viva.a: Because it is atraumatic; its smooth oval jaws hold the soft, vascular pregnant cervix securely without piercing or lacerating the tissue.

viva.q: How is sponge holding forceps used to inspect the cervix after an instrumental delivery?
viva.a: Two forceps are walked hand-over-hand clockwise around the entire cervical circumference to visualise all angles for lacerations.

image.brief: Full-length view of Rampley sponge holding forceps laid flat on a light grey background showing ratchet lock and serrated oval fenestrated jaws.

items.summary: An angulated biopsy instrument engineered to punch out clean, full-thickness tissue bites from the cervix.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Features long slender shanks that are angled at the grip to keep the operator hands below the examiner line of sight.
Jaws comprise a stationary hollow receiving cup and an upper mobile blade with a sharp cutting rim that bites into the base.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Obtaining directed cervical tissue samples when colposcopy reveals suspicious acetowhite epithelium or abnormal vascular patterns.
Investigating abnormal cervical cytology results, recurrent cervicitis, and unexplained post-coital bleeding.
Histological confirmation of suspected cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) or invasive cervical carcinoma.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Biopsy must be taken at the junction of normal and abnormal epithelium to assess invasion depth and tumour architecture.
Never biopsy the necrotic slough in the centre of a large tumour mass, as non-viable tissue precludes accurate histological diagnosis.

viva.q: Where on a suspicious cervical lesion should the punch biopsy be targeted?
viva.a: At the margin joining abnormal and healthy tissue, avoiding central necrosis to capture viable histological margins and invasion depth.

viva.q: Why is the shank of a punch biopsy forceps angled?
viva.a: The angulation drops the handle and surgeon hand away from the line of vision through the vaginal speculum.

image.brief: Cervical punch biopsy forceps on a neutral background showing pistol-grip handle, bayonet shank, and sharp rectangular cutting jaw mechanism.

items.summary: A long, malleable graduated metallic probe with a blunt tip used to assess the direction and length of the uterocervical cavity.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Malleable metallic instrument measuring approximately 12 inches (30 cm) in total length with a flat textured handle.
Features an angulation of about 30 degrees situated 2 inches from the tip to align with the normal anteversion of the uterus.
Calibrated in inches or centimetres along the shaft with a rounded, blunt olive tip.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Determining uterocervical length and direction (anteverted or retroverted) before intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) placement.
Assessing cavity depth before dilation and curettage (D&C), endometrial biopsy, and medical termination of pregnancy (MTP).
Sounding a suspected uterine polyp or missing intrauterine device string.
Differentiating a pedunculated fibroid polyp from uterine inversion, and measuring supravaginal elongation of the cervix in prolapse.
Used during pelvic radiography (anteroposterior and lateral views) to locate displaced missing intrauterine devices.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: If the sound advances significantly beyond the bimanual uterine estimate, immediately suspect uterine perforation.
Sims olive-pointed graduated sound features a bulbous nodular tip specifically designed to dilate a stenosed internal os.
The sound should always be introduced with gentle tactile precision without forceful pushing.

viva.q: What clinical warning sign indicates uterine perforation during sounding?
viva.a: The sound passes smoothly beyond the estimated bimanual uterine fundal distance without encountering the normal resistance of the fundus.

viva.q: Why does the Sims sound have a thirty-degree curve two inches from the tip?
viva.a: The angulation corresponds to the normal anatomical angle between the cervical canal and the anteverted uterine body.

image.brief: Straight-on view of a nickel-plated Sims uterine sound on a plain background showing calibrated markings along the shaft and terminal 30-degree bend.

items.summary: A smooth, solid steel probe with a gentle continuous curve and no calibrations, used to explore the bladder boundaries.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Solid stainless steel instrument featuring a gentle continuous curvature towards its blunt rounded tip.
Distinct from a uterine sound by having no calibrations, no angular bend, and a thicker, smoother profile.
Available in multiple surgical gauges and lengths.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Delineating the inferior anatomical extent of the urinary bladder and cystocele during vaginal hysterectomy and pelvic floor repairs.
Measuring urethral and bladder length and identifying bladder base position before making vaginal mucosal incisions.
Acting as an emergency blunt urethral dilator in mild urethral strictures.
Can serve as an emergency metallic guide to locate the urethral passage when catheterisation is difficult.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Distinguished from a female metal catheter by being completely solid, lacking any drainage lumen or lateral eyelets.
Gentle handling is critical to avoid creating a false urethral passage or puncturing a thinned bladder wall.

viva.q: How do you distinguish a bladder sound from a female metal catheter?
viva.a: The bladder sound is a completely solid metallic rod without markings or lumen, whereas the female catheter is hollow with drainage eyelets.

viva.q: What is the surgical purpose of introducing a bladder sound during vaginal hysterectomy?
viva.a: It identifies the inferior boundary and reflection of the bladder base, protecting it from accidental incision during anterior colpotomy.

image.brief: Polished steel bladder sound shown horizontally on white background exhibiting a gentle curve towards the blunt tip and solid uncalibrated shaft.

items.summary: A silicone or rubber prosthetic device placed in the vagina to support prolapsed pelvic organs or manage urinary incontinence.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Moulded prosthetic device manufactured from medical-grade silicone, flexible polyvinyl chloride, or soft rubber.
Available in support types (ring, ring with support, incontinence dish) and space-occupying types (Gellhorn, cube, donut, Gehrung, Hodge).

blocks.title: Indications
bullets: Conservative management of uterine prolapse, vaginal vault prolapse, cystocele, and rectocele.
Patients unfit for pelvic reconstruction due to severe cardiovascular or pulmonary comorbidities, or advanced age.
Temporary relief in women awaiting scheduled surgery, during puerperal prolapse, or in early pregnancy up to 16 weeks gestation.
Women desiring future childbearing who wish to defer definitive surgical correction.
Management of symptomatic stress urinary incontinence and symptomatic retroverted uterus.

blocks.title: Adverse effects and complications
bullets: Erosion of the vaginal epithelium with persistent foul discharge, postmenopausal bleeding, and ulceration.
Neglected or forgotten pessary leading to impaction, incarceration, and vesicovaginal or rectovaginal fistula.
Interference with coitus: space-occupying designs (Gellhorn, cube, donut) prevent vaginal intercourse.

blocks.title: Contraindications
bullets: Uninvestigated abnormal vaginal bleeding.
Active pelvic or vaginal infection including acute vaginitis.
Suspected or confirmed malignancy of the cervix, vagina, or vulva.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Insertion technique: collapsed between fingers and guided into the posterior fornix with the opposite side resting behind the pubic notch.
Cube pessaries generate negative suction and are especially effective when poor perineal body tone causes ring pessaries to fall out.
Hodge and Smith pessaries are specifically contoured to support and antevert a symptomatic retroverted uterus.
Patients require follow-up every 3 months for removal, mucosal inspection, cleaning, and reinsertion.

viva.q: What are the two major functional categories of vaginal pessaries?
viva.a: Support pessaries (such as ring and incontinence dish) which rely on pelvic floor shelves, and space-occupying pessaries (Gellhorn, donut, cube).

viva.q: What severe complication arises from a neglected, forgotten vaginal pessary?
viva.a: Vaginal mucosal erosion, severe chronic infection, impaction, and progression to vesicovaginal or rectovaginal fistula.

viva.q: Why must sexually active women be counselled before choosing a Gellhorn or donut pessary?
viva.a: Space-occupying pessaries completely occlude the vaginal canal, making sexual intercourse impossible while the device is in place.

image.brief: Assortment of vaginal pessaries including a flexible silicone ring pessary, a Gellhorn pessary with central stem, and a perforated cube pessary on white background.

items.summary: A heavy, non-ratcheted stainless steel transfer forceps used to transfer sterile instruments and surgical supplies aseptically.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Heavy stainless steel instrument with wide finger rings, long straight shanks, and no ratchet lock.
Jaws are heavily built and curved downward with transverse gripping ridges to securely hold slippery metallic tools.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Transferring sterile instruments from boilers, autoclaves, or storage drums into sterile procedural trays.
Removing sterile instruments from storage jars without contaminating remaining contents.
Dispensing sterile cotton balls, gauze rolls, and surgical dressing packs during clinical procedures.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Stored in a dedicated antiseptic jar with tips pointing downward; the jaws must never touch unsterile rims or surfaces.
The lack of a ratchet prevents accidental locking, allowing quick one-handed pickup and release.

viva.q: What is the primary clinical purpose of Cheatle forceps?
viva.a: It is an aseptic transfer forceps used to pick up and transfer sterile instruments and dressing packs without contaminating them.

viva.q: Why do Cheatle forceps lack a ratchet lock?
viva.a: To permit rapid, effortless grasping and release of heavy sterile instruments with one hand without mechanical jamming.

image.brief: Stainless steel Cheatle forceps resting on a surgical towel showing long parallel shanks, finger rings without ratchet, and broad curved serrated jaws.

items.summary: A rigid, trumpet-shaped monaural acoustic stethoscope used for auscultating foetal heart sounds over the maternal abdomen.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Hollow, rigid funnel or trumpet made of lightweight aluminium, stainless steel, or polished wood.
Features a broad circular base that rests flat on the maternal abdomen and a narrow flat disc earpiece for the examiner ear.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Auscultating foetal heart sounds during antenatal check-ups and intrapartum surveillance.
Placed perpendicularly over the maternal abdomen over the site corresponding to the foetal back.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Must be held perpendicularly against the abdominal wall without touching the instrument with hands, to avoid friction noise.
Simultaneously palpate maternal radial pulse to differentiate foetal heart sounds from maternal arterial pulsation.

viva.q: Where on the maternal abdomen should the Pinard stethoscope be placed?
viva.a: Over the maternal abdominal wall overlying the foetal back, where foetal cardiac vibrations conduct with greatest clarity.

viva.q: Why must the clinician remove their hand from the Pinard stethoscope while auscultating?
viva.a: Hand contact creates acoustic friction artefacts that drown out the faint, high-frequency foetal heart sounds.

image.brief: Metallic tubular Pinard foetal stethoscope standing vertically on a plain surface showing wide abdominal bell and flat circular earpiece.

items.summary: An electronic handheld ultrasound device using continuous-wave Doppler ultrasound to detect and display foetal heart rate.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Portable battery-operated electronic console connected by a coiled cable to an ultrasound transducer probe.
Transducer incorporates piezoelectric crystals that generate high-frequency ultrasound waves.
Equipped with a built-in loudspeaker and a digital liquid-crystal screen displaying foetal heart rate in beats per minute.

blocks.title: Principles and method
bullets: Operates on the Doppler principle: reflected sound waves from moving foetal heart valves and myocardium undergo a frequency shift.
Reflected acoustic shifts are processed into audible sounds resembling galloping horses and computed digitally.
Acoustic coupling gel is applied to the maternal abdomen overlying the foetal back, and the transducer is angled until signals are clear.

blocks.title: Advantages and limitations
bullets: Advantages: portable, rapid, reassures parents, provides clear digital readouts during outpatient check-ups.
Limitations: false reassurance during home use, difficulty picking up signals in maternal obesity, polyhydramnios, or unstable foetal lie.

viva.q: What physical principle underlies the function of a handheld foetal Doppler?
viva.a: The Doppler effect: high-frequency ultrasound emitted by piezoelectric crystals undergoes a frequency shift upon reflecting off moving cardiac structures.

viva.q: Why is coupling gel necessary when using a foetal Doppler probe?
viva.a: Coupling gel eliminates air pockets between transducer and maternal skin, preventing reflection of ultrasound waves at tissue boundaries.

image.brief: Compact battery-powered foetal Doppler device with digital display screen, attached ultrasound probe resting in holster on a white background.

items.summary: A contoured wooden or plastic scraping spatula designed to collect exfoliative ectocervical cells for conventional cytology.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Disposable flat spatula crafted from birchwood or medical-grade plastic with two distinct contoured working ends.
Features an asymmetrical lobed contour at one end with a central projecting tip and lateral curved shoulder.
Opposite end is broad and rounded, used for vaginal fornix or vaginal wall scraping.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Sampling ectocervical exfoliated cells for conventional Papanicolaou (Pap) smear screening.
Collecting specimens from the lower third of the endocervical canal and vaginal fornix for microbiological evaluation.
Used in dermatology and gynaecology clinics for superficial mucosal scrapings.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Sampling technique: the central projection is inserted into the external os and rotated through a full 360-degree sweep.
The harvested cells are smeared across a glass slide and immediately fixed with 95% ethyl alcohol spray or immersion.
Alternative cervical screening methods include liquid-based cytology (LBC), visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), and HPV DNA testing.

viva.q: How is the Ayre spatula positioned and rotated during a Pap smear?
viva.a: The longer contour is inserted into the external os while the shoulder sweeps the ectocervix through a complete 360-degree rotation.

viva.q: Why must the glass slide be fixed immediately after spreading the cervical scrape?
viva.a: Immediate fixation with 95% ethyl alcohol prevents air-drying artefacts that distort cellular morphology and obscure nuclear details.

image.brief: Birchwood Ayre spatula shown horizontally on white paper, detailing the characteristic notched contour of the sampling tip.

items.summary: A soft bristled conical or broom-shaped sampler engineered to harvest cells from the endocervical canal and transformation zone.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Comprises a slender flexible plastic shaft with a conical bristled brush head or triangular broom configuration.
Bristles are soft and atraumatic to harvest cellular clusters without causing stromal bleeding.
In broom configurations, longer central bristles penetrate the canal while outer flexible bristles sweep the ectocervix.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Sampling the endocervical canal and transformation zone for cervical cancer screening and human papillomavirus (HPV) testing.
Essential sampling tool for liquid-based cytology platforms.
Superior to spatulas in postmenopausal women whose squamocolumnar junction has migrated deeply into the endocervical canal.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Technique: inserted into endocervical canal and rotated gently through 180 degrees, or 4 to 5 times for broom devices.
Excessive or forceful rotation must be avoided to prevent traumatic bleeding that obscures cytology with excess red blood cells.
Fixative solution or spray used for slide preparation contains 95% ethyl alcohol.

viva.q: Why is a cytobrush preferred over an Ayre spatula in postmenopausal women?
viva.a: Because estrogen deficiency causes the squamocolumnar junction to recede into the endocervical canal, where only a bristled brush can reach.

viva.q: How is the sample handled after using a cervical broom for liquid-based cytology?
viva.a: The broom head is swirled vigorously in the preservative fluid vial or snapped off directly into the vial to capture all harvested cells.

image.brief: Endocervical cytobrush with blue conical bristle tip and plastic handle alongside a triangular broom sampler on a sterile background.

items.summary: A grooved glass or plastic container used to hold and fix glass microscope slides immersed in preservative fluid.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Upright cylindrical or rectangular jar with internal vertical grooves designed to hold microscope slides upright.
Equipped with a secure screw cap or lid to prevent evaporation of volatile fixative alcohol.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Transporting freshly prepared cervical cytology smear slides from the clinical examination room to the pathology laboratory.
Fixing exfoliative cytology smears in 95% ethyl alcohol immediately after smear collection.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Filled with 95% ethyl alcohol as standard fixative for conventional Papanicolaou smears.
Slides must be immersed immediately without allowing the wet smear to dry out in atmospheric air.

viva.q: What fixative solution is placed inside a Coplin jar for cervical Pap smears?
viva.a: Ninety-five percent ethyl alcohol is the standard fixative solution used to immerse and preserve the cellular smear.

viva.q: Why must cervical smear slides be placed immediately into the fixative?
viva.a: To prevent air-drying artefacts, which cause cellular swelling, nuclear distortion, and loss of diagnostic chromatin details.

image.brief: Rectangular plastic Coplin staining jar with slotted vertical internal grooves and screw cap on a plain white laboratory bench.

items.summary: A cervical screening method where exfoliated cells scraped from the squamocolumnar junction are spread directly onto a glass slide.

blocks.title: Method and procedure
bullets: Decontaminate and gently wipe excessive mucus or blood from the ectocervix using a dry gauze swab.
Insert the longer projection of the Ayre spatula into the external os and rotate firmly through 360 degrees.
Immediately spread the collected scrapings onto a clean glass slide using two smooth longitudinal strokes.
Apply 95% ethyl alcohol fixative spray held approximately 30 cm away from the slide, or immerse in a Coplin jar.
Package slide securely with requisition details and transport to the cytopathology laboratory for reporting.

blocks.title: Classification systems
bullets: Papanicolaou classification grades smears from Class I (normal) to Class V (invasive malignant cells).
The 2001 Bethesda system categorises findings into negative for intraepithelial lesion, ASCUS, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL, and malignancy.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Immediate fixation within seconds is paramount to avoid drying artefacts that degrade nuclear details.
Scraping must encompass the squamocolumnar junction where pre-invasive neoplastic transformation originates.

viva.q: What is the critical timing step after applying a cervical scrape to a glass slide?
viva.a: Immediate fixation with ninety-five percent ethyl alcohol within seconds, preventing air drying that destroys diagnostic cellular morphology.

viva.q: What anatomical site must the Ayre spatula sample during a Pap smear?
viva.a: The transformation zone and squamocolumnar junction, where neoplastic dysplasia most frequently originates.

image.brief: Clinical diagram illustrating cervical Pap smear collection: Ayre spatula rotated 360 degrees at the cervical os with slide preparation steps.

items.summary: A modern cervical cytology method where collected cells are rinsed into liquid preservative for automated thin-layer processing.

blocks.title: Principles and technology
bullets: Harvested cervical cells from a cytobrush or broom device are transferred directly into a preservative liquid medium.
Cellular suspension undergoes filtration or centrifugation and density-gradient sedimentation.
Cells are deposited as an even, monolayer thin-film on a glass slide, virtually free of obscuring blood and mucus.

blocks.title: Comparison of ThinPrep and SurePath
bullets: ThinPrep: brush is rinsed in methanol preservative; sample is filtered and transferred by controlled vacuum pressure over a 2 cm circle.
SurePath: broom head is detached and left in ethanol preservative; processed by centrifugation and sedimentation over a 1.3 cm circle.

blocks.title: Advantages over conventional Pap smear
bullets: Substantially reduces unsatisfactory sample rates from 9-10% down to 1-2%.
Eliminates obscuring background mucus, red blood cells, and inflammatory debris.
Residual liquid specimen can be utilised for reflex high-risk HPV testing, Chlamydia, and Neisseria gonorrhoeae PCR assays.
Higher diagnostic sensitivity for detecting low-grade and high-grade cervical squamous intraepithelial lesions.

blocks.title: Limitations
bullets: Higher cost of automated processing equipment and specialised preservative transport vials.
Requires specialised laboratory personnel and automated cytocentrifuges or filtration processors.

viva.q: What are the two major commercial systems for liquid-based cervical cytology?
viva.a: ThinPrep, which utilises methanol fixative and membrane filtration, and SurePath, which uses ethanol preservative with density-gradient centrifugation.

viva.q: What is the primary diagnostic advantage of liquid-based cytology over conventional Pap smear?
viva.a: It produces a clean monolayer of cells free from obscuring blood, mucus, and inflammatory exudate, lowering unsatisfactory rates to 1-2%.

viva.q: What auxiliary tests can be run on residual fluid from a liquid-based cytology vial?
viva.a: Molecular testing for high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes, Chlamydia trachomatis, and Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

image.brief: Schematic representation comparing automated liquid-based cytology workflow (vial, filtration, and monolayer slide) with conventional smear technique.

items.summary: A double-ended metallic curette featuring a sharp fenestrated loop on one end and a blunt loop on the other.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Long metallic instrument with a central handle shank and two distinct fenestrated oval loops.
One end features a sharp scraping cutting edge for gynaecological procedures.
The opposite end possesses a smooth, rounded blunt rim for obstetric indications.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Sharp end: fractional curettage, endometrial sampling in abnormal uterine bleeding, postmenopausal bleeding, and endometrial hyperplasia.
Curetting the base of a pedicle following cervical or endometrial polypectomy.
Investigating secondary amenorrhoea or infertility to obtain tissue to exclude endometrial tuberculosis.
Blunt obstetric end: evacuating retained products of conception in incomplete miscarriage, missed miscarriage, or postpartum haemorrhage.

blocks.title: Complications and cautions
bullets: Uterine perforation, cervical laceration, and heavy haemorrhage.
Over-vigorous curettage can cause Asherman syndrome by destroying the basal endometrium.
Damage to the decidua basalis in reproductive-age women increases the risk of placenta praevia in future pregnancies.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Sharp curette is used for firm, non-gravid gynaecological tissue; blunt curette is used for the soft, vascular pregnant uterus.
Modern outpatient endometrial sampling has largely transitioned to Pipelle curettage due to lower risk of perforation.

viva.q: Why is the blunt end of the Sims curette preferred in obstetric cases?
viva.a: The pregnant or puerperal myometrium is exceptionally soft and vascular; a sharp curette easily slices through the wall, causing uterine perforation.

viva.q: What severe long-term complication can result from vigorous curettage of the endometrial cavity?
viva.a: Asherman syndrome, resulting from destruction of the basal endometrium, secondary intrauterine synechiae, and resultant amenorrhoea or subfertility.

image.brief: Sims double-ended uterine curette shown on white surgical background displaying both the sharp fenestrated gynaecological scoop and blunt rounded obstetric loop.

items.summary: A rigid metallic cannula with a serrated side-cutting fenestration and removable stylet used with syringe suction for endometrial sampling.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Rigid, slender stainless steel tubular cannula with a blunt rounded tip and an oval lateral fenestration with serrated cutting edges.
Equipped with an internal metallic wire stylet to clear the lumen and a proximal Luer mount for syringe attachment.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Outpatient endometrial sampling for investigating abnormal uterine bleeding and postmenopausal bleeding.
Sampling thickened endometrium identified on pelvic ultrasonography without requiring general anaesthesia.
Evaluating endometrial histology to exclude endometrial tuberculosis in secondary amenorrhoea and unexplained infertility.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: A 10 mL or 20 mL syringe is attached to create negative pressure suction while scraping the uterine wall.
Largely superseded by flexible disposable polypropylene Pipelle curettes, which cause less discomfort and lower perforation risk.
Drawbacks include patient cramping, procedural pain, risk of uterine perforation, and occasionally insufficient tissue yield.

viva.q: How is suction generated when using a Novak biopsy curette?
viva.a: An external syringe is attached to the proximal end of the metallic cannula and pulled to create negative suction during curettage.

viva.q: Why has the Novak curette been largely replaced by the Pipelle device?
viva.a: The Pipelle is flexible, causes significantly less pain, creates its own suction without external syringes, and has a lower risk of perforation.

image.brief: Stainless steel Novak endometrial biopsy cannula with removable wire stylet and lateral cutting aperture displayed against a neutral background.

credit.generated: Illustration created with MaiK (StewardMD AI) and checked against the real instrument shape

items.summary: A flexible, disposable polypropylene suction curette with an internal piston used for outpatient endometrial sampling.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Flexible, transparent polypropylene cannula measuring 3.1 mm in outer diameter with a rounded, blunt tip.
Contains a snugly fitting internal solid plunger or stylet that slides within the outer graduated sheath.
Features a single lateral circular opening near the blunt distal tip.

blocks.title: Procedure and mechanism
bullets: Introduced gently through the cervical canal until the blunt tip reaches the uterine fundus.
The inner piston is retracted smoothly to the proximal end, creating negative suction inside the lumen.
The cannula is rotated 360 degrees while being moved back and forth between fundus and internal os to draw in endometrial strips.

blocks.title: Advantages and limitations
bullets: Advantages: rapid outpatient procedure, requires no anaesthesia or cervical dilation, highly cost-effective, minimal discomfort.
Significantly lower risk of uterine perforation compared to rigid metallic curettes.
Limitations: cannot reliably sample focal intra-cavitary lesions such as endometrial polyps or submucosal fibroids.

viva.q: How does the Pipelle curette create suction without an external syringe?
viva.a: Withdrawing the tight-fitting inner plunger creates a negative pressure vacuum within the calibrated polypropylene tube.

viva.q: What is a major diagnostic limitation of blind Pipelle endometrial sampling?
viva.a: It may miss focal intrauterine pathologies like endometrial polyps or submucosal fibroids, which require direct hysteroscopic visualisation.

image.brief: Flexible clear polypropylene Pipelle curette showing outer sheath with cm calibrations, internal drawn-back plunger, and distal side-sampling aperture.

items.summary: A long non-ratcheted surgical forceps with spoon-shaped fenestrated jaws designed to extract conception products without crushing.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Long instrument with scissor-type finger rings, long shanks, and completely non-ratcheted handles.
Jaws terminate in smooth, spoon-shaped or heart-shaped fenestrated cups without any teeth or transverse serrations.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Extracting loose gestational products, gestational sac, and decidual fragments in incomplete miscarriage.
Removing retained placental fragments and membranes during surgical management of secondary postpartum haemorrhage.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Crucially distinguished from sponge holding forceps by having no ratchet lock and no serrations on its spoon jaws.
Absence of a lock prevents forceful crushing and allows tactile sensing to minimise the risk of perforating myometrium.
Must be opened, closed, and rotated gently within the uterine cavity; blind grasping can grip the uterine wall or intestines.

viva.q: How do you distinguish an ovum forceps from a sponge holding forceps?
viva.a: Ovum forceps lacks a ratchet lock and has smooth non-serrated spoon-shaped fenestrated jaws, whereas sponge holding forceps is ratcheted with serrations.

viva.q: Why is the ovum forceps deliberately engineered without a ratchet lock?
viva.a: The lack of a lock prevents crushing of uterine tissue and allows the surgeon to feel resistance, reducing the risk of gripping the uterine wall.

image.brief: Full view of Heywood Smith ovum forceps resting on a blue drape showing ring handles without ratchet and smooth cupped fenestrated jaws.

credit.generated: Illustration created with MaiK (StewardMD AI) and checked against the real instrument shape

items.summary: A slightly curved, double-ended cylindrical metallic dilator used to sequentially dilate the internal cervical os.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Smooth, solid stainless steel rod with a gentle curve and blunt, slightly tapered rounded ends.
Typically double-ended, with each end bearing a different calibrated diameter stamped in millimetres (ranging from 1 mm to 20 mm).
Slight angulation facilitates gentle passage through the internal os along the axis of uterine flexion.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Gradual dilation of the cervical canal and internal os prior to fractional curettage, D&C, or operative hysteroscopy.
Dilation prior to insertion of intrauterine devices (IUCD, Mirena) when the internal os is tight or stenosed.
Dilation prior to surgical evacuation for missed miscarriage, septic miscarriage, or medical termination of pregnancy.
Relieving pathological cervical stenosis and facilitating drainage of pyometra or haematometra.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Dilators must be advanced sequentially in half-millimetre or millimetre increments without skipping sizes.
The instrument must be held like a pen, resting the fingers on the perineum as a guard against sudden fundal perforation.
Hawkins-Ambler dilator was an older alternative with a single tapered end and a broad disc handle.

viva.q: How should a Hegar dilator be held by the clinician during cervical dilation?
viva.a: It should be held like a pen, resting the fingers on the perineum to control forward momentum and prevent sudden fundal perforation.

viva.q: What is the primary danger of forcefully skipping dilator sizes during cervical dilation?
viva.a: Forced dilation can cause cervical laceration, severe haemorrhage, false passage formation, or cervical incompetence in future pregnancies.

image.brief: Set of graduated double-ended metallic Hegar dilators arranged in ascending diameters on a surgical tray with stamped millimetre markings visible.

items.summary: A reusable handheld plastic aspiration syringe fitted with self-locking valve buttons to generate vacuum for early uterine evacuation.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Comprises a plastic syringe barrel, an inner plunger with pull-ring handle, and double valve buttons with a locking clasp.
When the plunger is pulled back and the valve buttons click into position, a negative vacuum is stored.

blocks.title: Definition and timing
bullets: Menstrual regulation is the evacuation of endometrial contents within 14 days of a missed menstrual period.
Optimal clinical window is between 35 and 45 days counted from the first day of the last normal menstrual period.

blocks.title: Advantages
bullets: Simple, portable outpatient procedure that does not require electric power or noisy suction machines.
Performed under local paracervical block or no anaesthesia, offering lower complications and low procedural cost.

blocks.title: Complications and cautions
bullets: Failure to evacuate the pregnancy, resulting in continuation of pregnancy or incomplete abortion.
Rare risks include cervical laceration, uterine perforation, post-procedure endometritis, and vasovagal reaction.

viva.q: What is the operational timeframe for performing menstrual regulation using an MR syringe?
viva.a: Within fourteen days of a missed menstrual period, ideally between thirty-five and forty-five days from the first day of the last menstrual period.

viva.q: How is negative vacuum established in a menstrual regulation syringe before insertion?
viva.a: The plunger is fully withdrawn until the locking clasp buttons snap into place, storing negative pressure inside the closed cylinder.

image.brief: Handheld plastic menstrual regulation syringe showing transparent barrel, plunger pull-ring, dual valve buttons, and nozzle connector on clean backdrop.

credit.generated: Illustration created with MaiK (StewardMD AI) and checked against the real instrument shape

items.summary: A semi-rigid plastic cannula with opposed lateral apertures designed to connect with a manual vacuum aspiration syringe.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Semi-rigid medical-grade polyethylene tube with colour-coded adapters and size markings.
Features a rounded, atraumatic tip with two opposing offset lateral suction ports.
Proximal base has built-in wings or adapters to fit into the collar of a manual vacuum aspiration syringe.

blocks.title: Uses and advantages
bullets: Uterine evacuation for medical termination of pregnancy within 12 weeks of gestation and management of incomplete miscarriage.
High clinical success rate with significantly lower blood loss and pain compared to electric suction curettage.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Cannula size selected generally corresponds to gestational age in weeks.
Rotated 360 degrees and moved gently back and forth until a gritty sensation indicates complete uterine emptying.

viva.q: Up to what gestational limit is manual vacuum aspiration indicated for pregnancy termination?
viva.a: Manual vacuum aspiration is indicated for uterine evacuation within twelve weeks of gestation.

viva.q: What clinical signs indicate that the uterus has been completely emptied during manual vacuum aspiration?
viva.a: A characteristic gritty feeling against the cannula, uterine muscle contraction gripping the tube, and red or pink foam in the cannula.

image.brief: Set of colour-coded flexible plastic manual vacuum aspiration cannulas displayed with dual lateral eyes and adapter rings on sterile white field.

items.summary: A dehydrated stick of marine seaweed that swells by absorbing cervical secretions to achieve gradual hygroscopic cervical dilation.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Small, rigid cylindrical rod manufactured from dried, sterilised stems of the kelp Laminaria species.
Features an attached strong retrieval thread fastened securely to its distal outer end.
Swells radially 3 to 5 times its original size upon absorbing moisture from cervical secretions over several hours.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Gradual cervical dilation to induce abortion or induce labour in obstetric practice.
Cervical preparation before intrauterine procedures including operative hysteroscopy.

blocks.title: Complications and cautions
bullets: Maternal pelvic infection and potential neonatal or foetal infection.
Unpredictable dilation time and occasional failure to dilate the internal os.
Excess bleeding in incomplete abortion and risk of vasovagal shock or haemorrhagic shock.

viva.q: What is the biological source and mechanism of action of a Laminaria tent?
viva.a: Made from dehydrated Laminaria kelp stems, it absorbs moisture from cervical secretions and expands radially three to five-fold over several hours.

viva.q: What are the primary clinical advantages of hygroscopic cervical dilation over rapid mechanical dilation?
viva.a: It achieves gradual, uniform dilation without shearing force, greatly reducing the risk of cervical tears, uterine perforation, and cervical incompetence.

image.brief: Slender dried brown Laminaria tent rod showing retrieval string at proximal end beside an expanded, water-swollen tent on white background.

items.summary: A long, slender plastic rod terminating in a small sharp claw engineered to snag and rupture the foetal membranes.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Single-use plastic instrument with a long slender shaft and slightly curved distal end.
Distal end features a small, protected hook or claw that snags without sharp lateral cutting edges.
Designed to snag and tear the amniotic sac without inflicting trauma to the baby.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Artificial rupture of membranes (amniotomy) to induce labour or augment uterine contractions.
Checking the liquor to assess for meconium staining when foetal compromise is suspected.
Facilitating direct application of a foetal scalp electrode for continuous internal foetal monitoring.

blocks.title: Prerequisites and safety rules
bullets: Prerequisites: mother in active labour at term with the presenting part engaged in the maternal pelvis.
Risk of umbilical cord prolapse must be assessed and discussed prior to membrane rupture.
Modern alternative is the Amnicot or amniglove, a finger-cot featuring a miniature plastic hook on the fingertip.

viva.q: What essential clinical condition must be fulfilled before performing artificial rupture of membranes?
viva.a: The foetal presenting part must be well engaged in the maternal pelvis to prevent umbilical cord prolapse during fluid release.

viva.q: What should be assessed immediately following artificial rupture of membranes?
viva.a: Foetal heart rate must be auscultated to rule out cord compression or prolapse, and the colour and volume of liquor assessed.

image.brief: White plastic Amnihook showing full slender handle and close-up detail of the small curved recessed hook tip on a clinical background.

items.summary: A hollow, curved metallic cannula fitted with an adjustable conical rubber stopper used for tubal patency testing.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Hollow stainless steel cannula with a gentle distal curve and a proximal Luer mount for dye injection.
Equipped with a sliding conical rubber stopper that can be adjusted according to the length of the uterus.
Distal tip features 3 to 6 small holes to allow dye to disperse evenly into the uterine cavity.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Infusing radio-opaque contrast medium during hysterosalpingography (HSG) to evaluate tubal patency.
Checking tubal patency during diagnostic laparoscopy and chromopertubation.
Anteflexing the uterus during laparoscopic procedures to visualise the pouch of Douglas (POD), and manipulating the uterus sideways.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Alternative cannulas include Leech-Wilkinson cannula, Liddell cannula, and Cohen-Eder cannula.
The Leech-Wilkinson cannula is a straight tube-like instrument with a conical spiral end that can cause injury to the endocervix.

viva.q: What is the purpose of the conical rubber stopper on the Rubin cannula?
viva.a: It forms a tight seal against the external cervical os, preventing leakage of injected contrast dye into the vagina during HSG.

viva.q: How does the Rubin cannula assist during diagnostic laparoscopy?
viva.a: It allows injection of dye to check tubal patency and enables manipulation of the uterus to expose the pouch of Douglas.

image.brief: Curved metal Rubin cannula shown horizontally on a surgical tray with adjustable rubber cone and perforated distal tip.

items.summary: A straight ratcheted haemostatic forceps with transverse serrations used to clamp bleeding vessels and hold fascial edges.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Scissor-pattern instrument with straight tapered blades, looped finger handles, and an interlocking ratchet lock.
The inner surfaces of the blades feature transverse serrations along their entire length without an end tooth.
Available in small, medium, and long sizes to suit varying wound depths.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Grasping and securing bleeding vessels in superficial wound layers to achieve immediate haemostasis.
Holding structural tissue margins including rectus sheath fascia, aponeurosis, and peritoneum during laparotomy.
Used as an emergency clamp to hold a suture needle or guide a ligature.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Straight configuration is ideal for superficial planes and holding wound edges where direct straight traction is needed.
Crushing force can damage delicate muscular and neural structures if applied indiscriminately.

viva.q: What distinguishes straight artery forceps from curved artery forceps in clinical application?
viva.a: Straight artery forceps are primarily used to grasp fascial and peritoneal edges or superficial bleeders, whereas curved forceps target deep vessels.

viva.q: Why do the inner jaws of artery forceps have transverse serrations?
viva.a: Transverse serrations compress the lumen of the bleeding vessel securely without slicing through the vascular wall.

image.brief: Full-length straight stainless steel artery forceps shown open and closed on a white background displaying transverse serrations.

credit.title: Spencer Wells-type artery forceps, London, England, 1880-190 Wellcome L0058075.jpg
credit.author: Wellcome Collection

items.summary: A curved ratcheted haemostatic clamp designed to secure deep bleeding vessels and facilitate ligature placement.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Ratchet-locking instrument with finger rings and smoothly curved jaws carrying transverse serrations on the grasping surface.
The curve follows the surgeon line of vision, allowing tips to hook around bleeding vessels in deep pelvic cavities.
Available in various lengths, from delicate fine patterns to robust long clamps.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Clamping bleeding blood vessels in deep operative fields to arrest haemorrhage.
Under-running and applying ligatures around vascular pedicles with minimal visual obstruction.
Long curved varieties serve as pedicle clamps during hysterectomy to grasp, cut, and ligate uterine and ovarian ligaments.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: The curvature permits the ligature to slip effortlessly over the tip when tying off a vessel.
Excessive crushing of surrounding parenchymal tissue must be avoided to prevent necrosis.

viva.q: Why is the curved artery forceps preferred over straight forceps for ligating bleeders?
viva.a: The curved tip drops away from the visual field and allows the ligature loop to slide smoothly over the nose of the clamp.

viva.q: How are long curved clamps employed during abdominal hysterectomy?
viva.a: They are placed across supportive and vascular ligaments (infundibulopelvic, round, and cardinal ligaments) prior to transection.

image.brief: Curved stainless steel haemostatic forceps displayed on a surgical green cloth highlighting curved serrated tips and ratchet lock.

items.summary: The smallest variety of curved artery forceps with delicate fine jaws, engineered for precise haemostasis in confined spaces.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Miniature haemostatic forceps measuring approximately 12.5 cm in length with slender shanks and delicate finger rings.
Features fine, tapered, curved jaws with delicate transverse serrations extending to the tip.
Articulating multi-step ratchet allows graded locking on small individual vessels.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Securing fine pinpoint bleeders in delicate anatomical zones such as the perineum, vulva, and neonate.
Used during episiotomy repair, neonatal resuscitation procedures, and plastic reconstructive gynaecological surgery.
Tagging and holding fine suture strands without crimping or fraying the material.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: The smallest member of the artery forceps family.
Not intended for clamping heavy tissues or dense vascular pedicles, which can spring or bend the fine jaws.

viva.q: What is the defining anatomical characteristic of a Halsted mosquito forceps?
viva.a: It is the smallest variety of haemostatic forceps, featuring exceptionally fine, short, tapered curved jaws with transverse serrations.

viva.q: Where is mosquito forceps most frequently used in obstetrics and gynaecology?
viva.a: During episiotomy repair, vulvovaginal surgery, and delicate paediatric or neonatal procedures where pinpoint haemostasis is needed.

image.brief: Delicate Halsted mosquito forceps resting next to a metric rule showing miniature proportions and fine curved serrated tips.

items.summary: A robust ratcheted clamp with transverse serrations and interlocking 1x2 teeth at the blade tips to prevent tissue slip.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Sturdy, long-handled clamp with finger ring handles, a firm ratchet lock, and straight or curved heavy blades.
Blades bear transverse serrations along their inner length and terminate in sharp interlocking 1x2 teeth.
The male tooth on one tip seats into a corresponding female notch on the opposing tip to ensure non-slip grip.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Clamping tough, slippery vascular pedicles and deep bleeders that resist standard smooth clamps.
Grasping dense fibrous structures such as rectus sheath, fascia, scalp, palm, or sole tissues.
Clamping uterine vessels and parametrial tissue during hysterectomy.
Historically used as an emergency instrument to perforate membranes during artificial rupture of membranes.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Causes severe crush injury and puncture due to the terminal interlocking teeth; never apply to viscera or viable margins.
The aggressive grip prevents retraction of large transected vessels into retroperitoneal planes.

viva.q: What design feature distinguishes Kocher forceps from a standard Spencer Wells forceps?
viva.a: The presence of sharp interlocking one-by-two teeth at the tips of the transverse-serrated jaws, providing a non-slip grip.

viva.q: Why must Kocher forceps never be applied to hollow viscera such as bowel or bladder?
viva.a: The crushing jaws and terminal sharp teeth inflict full-thickness mechanical and vascular injury leading to necrosis and perforation.

image.brief: Straight Kocher forceps on white background with close-up inset demonstrating the 1x2 interlocking terminal teeth and serrated jaws.

items.summary: A ratcheted grasping forceps with wide expanding blades and multiple fine interlocking teeth designed to hold tough fascia.

blocks.title: How to recognise it
bullets: Scissor-type instrument with finger rings, multi-position ratchet lock, and blades that curve outward to enclose a space.
Jaws terminate in broad, flattened tips bearing multiple fine comb-like interlocking teeth (commonly 4x5 or 5x6 teeth).
Named after the American surgeon Oscar Huntington Allis.

blocks.title: Uses
bullets: Grasping and elevating the rectus sheath fascia during abdominal opening and closure.
Holding the vaginal vault angles during vault closure in abdominal or vaginal hysterectomy.
Holding tough fibrous tissues including aponeurosis, tendons, fascia, and wound skin edges.
Grasping diseased adnexa or tubo-ovarian masses during salpingo-oophorectomy, and occasionally serving as emergency drape clips.

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Considered semi-traumatic: suitable for tough fascia, but can cause crush injury and necrosis if used on delicate viscera.
The hollow space between the bowed shanks prevents crushing of intervening tissue bulk.

viva.q: What structures is the Allis tissue forceps specifically designed to hold?
viva.a: Tough, fibrous anatomical structures such as the rectus sheath, fascia, aponeurosis, and vaginal vault margins.

viva.q: Why is Allis forceps avoided on healthy bowel or fallopian tubes intended for preservation?
viva.a: The fine sharp interlocking teeth exert high focal pressure that crushes and lacerates delicate muscular walls.

image.brief: Allis tissue forceps displayed on a grey surgical background with jaws slightly separated to show fine comb-like interlocking teeth.
